Synopsis:
UK ministers and the Environment Agency are exploring a fundamental overhaul of water abstraction pricing, particularly targeting large industrial users who currently pay disproportionately little per litre the more they consume. Against a backdrop of drought conditions affecting ~27 million people across England and Wales, the article highlights systemic failures: industrial abstraction licences carry no value-of-water component, datacentres consume 6.6m litres of drinking-quality water daily (projected to triple by 2030), and England faces a potential 5bn litre/day supply deficit by 2055. Reform of pricing and licensing is in early-stage policy discussion.
